# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫵 👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a display showing "0", a yellow light, and three wires colored green, red, and blue. I cannot hear or touch it. Mute has signaled me with [✍ 🫵 👆], which likely means "write down" or "note this," but without audio, I don't know what to write or why. Blind can feel the bomb's physical properties (texture, shape, hidden switches) that I might miss visually, and they are the only one who can act.

My priority is to establish a channel with Blind so they can correlate their tactile findings with my visual observations. Since I cannot hear, I must rely on Blind speaking to me? No, I am Deaf. I cannot receive speech. Wait, the rules say: "You never receive speech." This is a critical constraint. If I cannot receive speech, how do I get information from Blind?

Let's re-read carefully:
- **Deaf**: See the bomb... Cannot Hear anything... You never receive speech.
- **Mute**: Read manual... Cannot Speak...
- **Blind**: Reach bomb... Cannot See...

If I cannot receive speech, then Blind's words do not reach me. Mute cannot speak. So how does information flow to me?
1. Mute can gesture to me. (Visual)
2. Can Blind gesture to me? The rules say Blind "Cannot See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed". It doesn't explicitly say Blind *cannot* make gestures, but usually, if you can't see, you don't know what to gesture unless taught. However, Blind *can* speak. But I can't hear.
3. Is there a way for Blind to communicate to Mute, who then communicates to me? Yes. Blind speaks -> Mute hears -> Mute gestures -> I see.

So, I need to tell Blind what I see, so Blind can verify it against their touch. But wait, if I speak to Blind, Blind *hears* me. That works. Blind receives my speech.
What do I want from Blind? I want them to confirm if there are any physical features I can't see (like a switch position or a cut wire end). Or perhaps just acknowledge the state.

However, the most immediate issue is interpreting Mute's gesture [✍ 🫵 👆]. "Write", "You/Point", "Up/Index". Maybe "Write down point 1"? Or "Note this"?

Since I have limited turns and no feedback loop from myself (I can't hear if I'm wrong), I should provide the full visual description to Blind immediately. This allows Blind to start working. I will also try to signal Mute to ask for help in decoding the situation, using valid symbols.

Valid symbols for asking/clarifying: `🤔` is NOT in the list. `❓` is NOT in the list.
The alphabet includes: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

To ask a question, maybe use `🤔` isn't allowed. How about `☝` (index up) often means "one" or "attention". `👆` means "up" or "this".
Maybe I should just focus on communicating with Blind first, as they are the actor.

I will describe the bomb to Blind.
I will gesture to Mute to indicate I am ready/listening/waiting for instructions, perhaps using `👋` (wave) or `🙏` (please/help).

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see Display 0, Yellow Light, Wires Green Red Blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed from yellow to green. This is a critical update that I must communicate immediately, as it likely indicates a change in the bomb's state or a response to an action (though I see no wires cut). Since Blind cannot see colors, they are unaware of this shift unless I tell them. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak; if Mute gestures to me again, I might learn what the green light signifies according to the manual, but for now, my priority is informing the actor (Blind) of the visual reality.

I will describe the current state to Blind: Display 0, Light Green, Wires Green/Red/Blue intact. I will also gesture to Mute asking for clarification on the meaning of the green light, using symbols that might represent "question" or "explain". Since there is no question mark symbol, `☝` (index up) often denotes "one" or "attention/question" in some contexts, or `🤔` isn't available. `✍` was used by Mute earlier. Maybe `👆` (pointing up) combined with `❓` (not available). Let's try `☝` and `🫵` (you) to ask Mute to explain? Or simply wait for Mute to act. Given the empty context, Mute hasn't responded yet. I'll stick to updating Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light changed to GREEN. Display still 0. Wires G R B intact.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🫵"])
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👉]

The light remains green, and the display is still 0. Mute has gestured `[🤟 👉]`. `🤟` (ILY sign) often represents "Love" or "I Love You", but in a puzzle context with limited symbols, it might be a specific code or simply pointing to something relevant. `👉` means "Right" or "Point Right".

Since I cannot hear Blind's speech, I must rely on Mute to translate information from the manual to me via gestures, or for Blind to communicate through actions that result in visual changes I can see. However, the most direct path is ensuring Blind knows the current state. The previous message to Blind was sent last turn; assuming they received it, they are working on it.

Mute's gesture `[🤟 👉]` is ambiguous without audio context. It could mean "Cut the right wire"? Or "Look right"? Given the wires are Green(1), Red(2), Blue(3), "Right" usually implies the highest index or physical rightmost. If physical layout is left-to-right 1-2-3, then 3 is right.

I should confirm the wire positions to Blind again if there's any doubt, but more importantly, I need to know if Mute is giving an instruction. Since I can't ask Mute verbally (they can't speak/hear? No, Mute *can* read manual, *cannot* speak. Can Mute hear? Rules say: "A listener who cannot see gets a blank... whoever can hear receives your words". Mute is not listed as deaf. So Mute *can* hear. But Mute *cannot* speak. So I can speak to Mute, and they will hear me, but they can only reply by gesturing.

If I speak to Mute asking "What does 🤟 👉 mean?", they might gesture back.
But Blind is the one acting. Does Blind know what to do? Blind needs to know if the green light implies a safe state or a trigger.

Let's assume the standard bomb defusal logic: Colors matter.
Display 0. Light Green.
Wires: G, R, B.

I will describe the situation to Blind again to ensure synchronization, and ask Mute for clarification on their gesture using speech (which Mute hears).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Clarify gesture: 🤟 👉. What action?")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is GREEN. Display 0. Wires: 1-Green, 2-Red, 3-Blue.")
```
